title: Chhath Puja 2026 Travel Guide for Bihar and UP
summary: Your Chhath Puja 2026 travel guide for Bihar and UP: the exact dates, the best ghat cities, bus routes from Delhi, and how to plan and book early.
body_markdown:
Chhath sets off one of the largest annual movements of people in India. Across Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh, and among the Purvanchali community in Delhi and other cities, families travel home for the four day festival in numbers that trains simply cannot absorb. If you are planning to be at a ghat this year, the travel is the part that needs the earliest thought.


## **What This Chhath Travel Guide Covers**


This guide sets out the Chhath Puja 2026 travel essentials: the exact festival dates, the ghat cities worth heading to across Bihar and UP, how the demand builds, and the routes and booking approach that make the journey manageable. The aim is a practical plan rather than a description of the rituals.


Because rail seats vanish months ahead, road travel carries a large share of this rush. You can check current routes and fares to the major hubs on the[Varanasi bus booking page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/varanasi-bus-booking-online) and plan the journey home well before the festival week.


# **Chhath Puja 2026 Travel: Dates, Destinations and How to Plan**


Chhath is tied to the sixth day of the lunar fortnight after Diwali, and the whole trip hinges on getting the dates and the demand pattern right. This guide walks through the 2026 schedule, the cities where the festival is most striking, the routes into Bihar and UP, and the practical steps that keep the journey smooth during the busiest travel week of the region’s year.


## **Chhath Puja 2026 Dates**


The festival runs across four days in November 2026. Nahay Khay falls on Friday, November 13. Kharna is on Saturday, November 14. The main Sandhya Arghya, the evening offering to the setting sun, is on Sunday, November 15. Usha Arghya, the morning offering to the rising sun, closes the festival on Monday, November 16.


For most travellers, the two dates that matter are November 15 and 16. The Sunday evening and Monday morning offerings are the heart of the festival, and they fall together as a natural long weekend when the Monday holiday is counted. That combination is exactly what drives the travel surge in the days before.


## **Why Chhath Is the Biggest Travel Window for Bihar and UP**


Nothing else moves people back to Bihar and eastern UP the way Chhath does. It is a family festival observed at home, at the ghat where a household has always gone, so being physically present matters in a way it does not for many other holidays. That is why the demand is so concentrated and so hard to book late.


Trains fill first and fastest, often months in advance, and waitlists during this week are notoriously long. This is where road travel earns its place, since intercity buses add capacity on the Delhi to Bihar and Delhi to UP corridors when the railways are saturated. For anyone who missed the train booking window, the bus is usually the realistic way home.


## **The Long Weekend and How Demand Builds**


The travel demand does not peak on the festival dates themselves. It peaks in the days just before, as people reach their hometowns in time for Kharna and the Sandhya Arghya. Expect the heaviest outbound rush from roughly November 11 to 14, with the return travel spreading out after the Usha Arghya on November 16.


Planning around this pattern is half the battle. If you travel on the exact peak days, you pay more and choose from less. Booking a seat for a date a little ahead of the crush, and planning the return for midweek after the 16th rather than the immediate Monday evening, makes the whole Chhath Puja 2026 travel plan easier on both cost and comfort.


## **Best Places to Observe Chhath in Bihar and UP**


Patna sits at the centre of it. The Ganga ghats through the city, from Gandhi Ghat onward, host enormous, organised gatherings for the Arghya offerings, and the scale there is unlike anywhere else. It is the definitive Chhath city.


Beyond the capital, several cities stand out for anyone building a Chhath Puja 2026 travel plan around the ghats. Varanasi’s riverfront needs no introduction and takes on a particular character during the festival. Prayagraj offers the Sangam, Ayodhya the Saryu, and Gaya the Falgu, each with its own gathering. In eastern UP, Gorakhpur along the Rapti and the ghats around Lucknow’s Gomti draw large local crowds. Each of these is reachable by road, which matters when the trains are full.


## **Planning Your Chhath Travel: Routes and Booking**


The core corridors run out of Delhi and the NCR, where a large Purvanchali population travels home each year. The routes that carry the Chhath rush include Delhi to Patna, Delhi to Varanasi, Delhi to Gorakhpur and Delhi to Lucknow, most of them run as overnight journeys so you reach the ghat city by morning.


A few comforts help on a long overnight leg. On select routes such as Delhi to Varanasi, Delhi to Lucknow and Delhi to Gorakhpur, the Food on Bus service lets you pre book a meal at checkout, and the Freemeal coupon applies on the Delhi to Lucknow and Delhi to Gorakhpur routes. You can check current schedules and fares on the[Gorakhpur bus booking page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/gorakhpur-bus-booking-online) or the[Lucknow bus booking page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/lucknow-bus-booking-online) before you fix the date. Given the demand, booking early is not caution, it is the difference between travelling on your chosen day and not travelling at all.


## **Practical Tips for Travelling During Chhath**


A few honest points make the trip smoother. Book well ahead, since seats on every mode tighten sharply in the week before the festival, and fares rise with demand. Travelling a day earlier than the peak is usually cheaper and far less crowded than the last outbound rush.


At the destination, expect ghat areas to be congested and many roads near the river closed to traffic on the Arghya evenings and mornings, so plan local movement with extra time. Carry a valid government photo ID for any intercity booking. If you are on an overnight bus, the standard safety features help, with GPS live tracking through the app, female friendly seating and a two driver rotation on the longer routes. Confirm current service availability on your specific route before assuming a particular comfort is offered.


## **Getting Home in Time**


Chhath rewards planning more than almost any other festival, because the whole point is to be present at the ghat on the right evening and morning. Miss the booking window and the trip gets harder and costlier at every step, so the earliest decision to make is simply the date you travel.


Fix that date, book the seat while there is still choice, and plan the return for after the Monday offering rather than into the immediate rush. With the journey settled early, the festival itself, the fasting, the river and the two Arghya offerings, is what the days are left free for.


## **Chhath Puja 2026 Travel: Common Questions**


The questions below cover what travellers most often check before heading home for the festival.


### **What are the exact Chhath Puja 2026 dates?**


Chhath Puja 2026 runs from November 13 to 16: Nahay Khay on the 13th, Kharna on the 14th, Sandhya Arghya on Sunday the 15th, and Usha Arghya on Monday the 16th.


### **When should I travel for Chhath Puja 2026?**


For Chhath Puja 2026 travel, aim to reach your ghat city by November 14 for Kharna and the Sunday Arghya. The heaviest rush runs from November 11 to 14.


### **Is Chhath 2026 a long weekend?**


Yes, the Sandhya Arghya on Sunday November 15 and the Usha Arghya on Monday November 16 fall together, and the Monday holiday makes it a natural long weekend for travel.


### **Which are the best places to observe Chhath in Bihar and UP?**


Patna’s Ganga ghats are the largest, followed by Varanasi, Prayagraj’s Sangam, Ayodhya’s Saryu, Gaya’s Falgu, and the ghats at Gorakhpur and Lucknow in eastern UP.


### **Why book a bus for Chhath instead of a train?**


Trains to Bihar and UP fill months ahead for Chhath, with long waitlists. Buses add capacity on the Delhi corridors, making road travel the realistic option for many families.


### **Which bus routes are busiest during Chhath?**


The busiest corridors run from Delhi and the NCR, including Delhi to Patna, Delhi to Varanasi, Delhi to Gorakhpur and Delhi to Lucknow, most operating as overnight journeys.


### **How far ahead should I book for Chhath travel?**


Book as early as you can, ideally several weeks ahead. Seats on every mode tighten sharply in the week before the festival, and fares climb steadily with the rising demand.


### **Are meals available on these overnight bus routes?**


On select routes such as Delhi to Varanasi, Delhi to Lucknow and Delhi to Gorakhpur, you can pre book a meal, and a Freemeal coupon applies on the Delhi to Lucknow and Delhi to Gorakhpur routes.


### **What should I expect at the ghats during Chhath?**


Expect large, organised crowds and many riverside roads closed to traffic on the Arghya evenings and mornings, so plan local travel with extra time and avoid driving close to the ghats.


### **When is the best time to return after Chhath?**


Returning midweek after the Usha Arghya on November 16, rather than the immediate Monday evening, spreads you clear of the return rush and usually means better fares and seats.


### **Is overnight bus travel safe during the festival rush?**


Overnight travel is manageable with the usual precautions. Look for GPS live tracking, female friendly seating and a two driver rotation on longer routes, and confirm the features on your specific service.


### **Do I need any documents to book a Chhath bus ticket?**


Carry a valid government photo ID for the booking and the journey. Keep it handy along with your ticket, since intercity travel during a high demand festival week involves frequent checks.
